SHAP boundarylogic use Shapley values, answer different questions: SHAP splits model’s predicted probability observation, relative average prediction training data. says score . boundarylogic measures distance decision boundary (globally) change alters decision (locally). says change decision change. chunks compute SHAP XGBoost models fastshap shapviz. run packages installed.
code: if (has_shap) {   # fastshap needs a prediction wrapper f(object, newdata) -> numeric vector;   # XGBoost needs the new data as an xgb.DMatrix.   pred_fn <- function(object, newdata) {     as.numeric(predict(object, xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(as.matrix(newdata))))   }    # Background and explanation data for each model   X_train_full <- bl_dat$train_data[,    bl_dat$var_names,    drop = FALSE]   X_train_v2   <- bl_dat_v2$train_data[, bl_dat_v2$var_names, drop = FALSE]   X_test_v2    <- bl_dat_v2$test_data[,  bl_dat_v2$var_names, drop = FALSE]    # The reduced model works in z-scores. SHAP is computed on those, but the   # plots show the feature values in raw units, as boundarylogic does.   to_raw <- function(X, scaling) {     X[] <- Map(function(x, v) x * scaling$scale[[v]] + scaling$center[[v]],                X, names(X))     X   }   X_train_v2_raw <- to_raw(X_train_v2, bl_results_v2$scaling)   X_test_v2_raw  <- to_raw(X_test_v2,  bl_results_v2$scaling)    # SHAP baseline: the mean predicted probability over the reduced model's   # training rows (fastshap does not attach one; shapviz needs it).   shap_baseline <- mean(pred_fn(xgb_fit_v2, X_train_v2)) }

title: CLAUDE.md — boundarylogic
text: boundarylogic R package operationalises PhD methodology post-hoc interpretability binary classification models. projects high-dimensional data 2D biplot (PCA CVA), approximates model’s decision boundary space, finds counterfactuals — minimum change observation flips prediction. Three-phase workflow: - Phase 1: data prep → model → biplot projection → prediction grid → bl_result (central anchor object) - Phase 2 (global): nearest boundary point per observation, surrogate model, robustness - Phase 3 (local): single-observation biplot rotation → counterfactual → Shapley attribution → sparse counterfactual bl_result object everything downstream consumes.

code: library(boundarylogic)  # Phase 1: prepare data, fit model, build biplot bl_dat <- bl_prepare_data(   data           = iris,   class_col      = "Species",   target_class   = "versicolor",   # 1 = versicolor, 0 = all others   train_fraction = 0.8,   seed           = 42L,   hull_fraction  = 0.9             # drop the outermost 10% of training points )  bl_mod <- bl_fit_model(   train_data = bl_dat$train_data,   var_names  = bl_dat$var_names,   model_type = "GLM" )  bl_results <- bl_build_result(   bl_data  = bl_dat,   bl_model = bl_mod,   method   = "PCA",   b_margin = 0.001                 # contour band: cutoff +/- 0.001 (the default) )  plot_biplotEZ(bl_results)  # Overlay test data test_pts <- bl_project_points(bl_results$test_data, bl_results) plot_biplotEZ(bl_results, points = test_pts) # Phase 2: global counterfactual search bl_bnd <- bl_find_boundary(bl_results) plot(bl_bnd)                   # jitter plot — per-variable distances + robustness plot(bl_bnd, type = "boxplot") # boxplot by confusion category  bl_sur <- bl_surrogate(bl_results) plot(bl_sur) # Phase 3: local interpretation of one observation pred_summary <- bl_predict(bl_results) tdp <- which(pred_summary$pred_class == 1)[1]   # first predicted class-1 row tgt <- bl_select_target(bl_results, target = tdp)  bl_local <- bl_find_local_cf(bl_results, tgt) plot(bl_local)  bl_shapley_values <- bl_shapley(bl_local) plot(bl_shapley_values)  bl_sparse <- bl_find_sparse_cf(bl_shapley_values) print(bl_sparse) plot(bl_sparse)
